artifacts.summary: Establishes that (C5) StabFaithful is finitary and decidable on the branching frame via total_eq_thread + truth_iff_mem, corrects the L-plus closure cost estimate from ~2,257 to ~250 lines, identifies a label-free SharingSkeleton factoring that reuses 1,065 landed lines, and sets out two viable architectures (full L-plus re-index vs. atomization) with a blocking user decision between them.

user_decision.question: Which datatype should (C5) StabFaithful be stated over: a new L-plus-indexed certificate that leaves the shipping JSON export contract untouched, or the existing Formula certificate run on an atomized target, which is ~4x cheaper but adds a field to the shipping certificate and states (C5) at Formula?
options: Route 1 - L-plus-indexed certificate over a label-free SharingSkeleton: ~2,400-3,900 new Lean lines in seven phases; shipping deterministic export contract unchanged in name, meaning and shape; (C5) stated natively over PlusFormula.stab.

Route 2 - atomization: run the existing Formula certificate on an expanded atomized target and constrain stab-atoms via a finite pairing; ~600-900 lines, zero re-indexing, all five existing conditions and decision procedures reused; but adds a pairing field to the shipping certificate (re-opens the JSON export contract additively) and states StabFaithful at Formula.
user_decision.recommended: Route 1 - L-plus-indexed certificate over a label-free SharingSkeleton: ~2,400-3,900 new Lean lines in seven phases; shipping deterministic export contract unchanged in name, meaning and shape; (C5) stated natively over PlusFormula.stab.
